item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 031124
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM PDT Thu Sep 3 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Karina, located well east of the Hawaiian Islands, on Hurricane
Lowell, located several hundred miles south of the Hawaiian Islands,
and on Hurricane Marie, located several hundred miles southwest of
the southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula.

Offshore of Southwestern Mexico:
An area of low pressure could form well offshore of southwestern
Mexico over the weekend or early next week. Gradual development is
possible, and the system could become a tropical depression around
the middle of next week while it moves west-northwestward at 10 to
15 mph, likely remaining well offshore of Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...40 percent.

$$
Forecaster Reinhart

WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 AM HST (1500 UTC), the center of Hurricane Karina was located
near latitude 19.8 North, longitude 136.7 West. Karina is moving
toward the west near 10 mph (17 km/h), with a more
west-northwestward motion expected over the next couple of days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 115 mph (185 km/h) with higher
gusts.  Karina is a category 3 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson
Hurricane Wind Scale. Gradual weakening is forecast during the next
several days.  However, Karina is expected to remain a hurricane for
the next couple of days.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 35 miles (55 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 125 miles
(205 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 961 mb (28.38 inches).

item.title: Hurricane Karina Forecast Discussion Number 29
item.description:
Issued at 500 AM HST Thu Sep 03 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 031437
TCDEP1
 
Hurricane Karina Discussion Number  29
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP112026
500 AM HST Thu Sep 03 2026
 
Little has changed in Karina's annular appearance over the last
several hours. The latest subjective Dvorak analysis from TAFB gave
an intensity estimate of 102 kt, while objective estimates from
CIMSS ranged from 90-95 kt. Given the continued downward trend
across subjective and objective Dvorak analysis, the initial
intensity estimate was set at 100 kt.
 
Karina's initial motion was set at 280/9 kt. The system is forecast
to shift more west-northwest over the next couple of days, as it
continues to be guided by a subtropical ridge to its north. By
late this weekend into early next week, an oncoming upper-level
trough is expected to pull Karina more to the northwest, away from
the main Hawaiian Islands. The official track forecast was little
changed from the previous advisory, with only slight adjustments
westward to reflect a blend of HCCA, GDMI, and the previous
official track forecast.
 
A steady weakening trend in Karina's intensity is still expected to
occur as the system encounters an increasingly drier mid-level
environment. After 24 h, Karina's weakening trend is
forecast to hasten as vertical wind shear increases and SSTs
decrease, with the system expected to become post-tropical by Day
4. The official intensity forecast increases the rate of weakening
compared to the previous advisory, falling just above most model
guidance within the first 24 h before landing closer to guidance
consensus thereafter.

MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...981 MB...28.97 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 AM MST (0900 UTC), the center of Hurricane Marie was located
near latitude 18.9 North, longitude 113.9 West. Marie is moving
toward the west-northwest near 10 mph (17 km/h), and this motion 
should continue for the next few days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 85 mph (140 km/h) with higher
gusts.  Some strengthening is forecast during the next 48 hours, 
and gradual weakening is anticipated to begin by this weekend.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 40 miles (65 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 205 miles
(335 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 981 mb (28.97 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Marie will affect portions of the coast of
southwest Mexico and the Baja California Peninsula for the next few
days and will likely spread northward to southern California over
the weekend.  These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf
and rip current conditions. Please consult products from your local
weather office. A depiction of rip current risk for the United
States can be found at:
hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep1.shtml?ripCurrents
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 AM MST.
 
$$

item.title: Hurricane Marie Forecast Discussion Number 9
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM MST Thu Sep 03 2026 
000
WTPZ43 KNHC 030856
TCDEP3
 
Hurricane Marie Discussion Number   9
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP132026
200 AM MST Thu Sep 03 2026

Marie continues to gradually become better organized, with very 
deep convection near the center and a more symmetric convective 
pattern.  Satellite estimates have slightly increased since the 
last advisory, and the initial intensity is set to 75 kt, closest 
to the latest TAFB fix.  

The intensity forecast for Marie is tricky.  While it still has a 
couple of days over warm waters with light shear, the structure 
remains somewhat broad, with a large outer wind field.  So far, 
this has prevented anything other than gradual strengthening.  It 
is still a bit curious why most of the guidance don't intensify 
this much during the next day or two, given the conducive 
large-scale environment.  While it is possible that Marie will be 
affected by the wake of Iselle, the forecast track could also be 
far enough away to miss the bulk of the cooler SSTs.  The new 
forecast is raised from the previous one, splitting the difference 
between the higher SHIPS/LGEM/rapid intensification guidance and 
the lower regional hurricane/corrected consensus models.  A steady 
weakening is likely after the system passes over colder waters in 
about 3 days.

Marie is moving west-northwestward at about 9 kt.  There are no 
changes to the previous synoptic pattern as this general course 
is anticipated to continue for the next several days due to a 
narrow ridge to the north.  While this ridge weakens later on, 
Marie should slow down a bit, but stay moving west-northwestward.  
The new forecast is close to an update of the last one, near a 
consensus of the Google DeepMind ensemble mean and the HFIP 
Corrected Consensus HCCA model.
